content:
alex: Heads-up — EU-West2 batch pool seeing a cluster of node restarts + GPU attach failures since ~04:10 UTC. Symptoms point to localized NVMe badblock clustering during the ephemeral cleaner run.
ops-bot: nvme-monitor ALERT: 12 nodes crossed SMART thresholds (reallocated sector count). Soft-offline actions triggered on devices.
mara: saw several `nvme io  - status: 0x01` logs and `blk_update_request: I/O error` in the attach path. GPUs failing with `device busy` on attach and attach timeouts (~25-35s).
jin: is this the same pattern as the last scrub-induced spike? any correlation with scrub schedule or GC waves?
alex: different timing — scrub started early (03:50) because backlog ramped overnight. We also had a small-file GC microburst from ephemeral cleanup that overlapped. IOPS on affected hosts spiked to ~240-260k for ~90s, queue depth saturated.
sam: suggestion: pause the cleaner on impacted hosts, drain GPUs (graceful), and mark nvme devices as read-only until we confirm no further reboots. Tradeoff: backlog in scheduling for ~1-3h vs preventing more node flapping.
leah: +1. Also push a temporary routing rule to avoid eu-west2 for latency-sensitive provisioning while we triage.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started automated drain for nodes: gnode-3561,g-3562,g-3588,g-3610,g-3622,g-3650,g-3667,g-3670,g-3679,g-3681,g-3690,g-3698.
mara: pulling dmesg snippets; posting minimal error extract for triage:
```
[  875.123456] nvme0: error: sq 1 cq 1 - submission timeout, aborting
[  875.123458] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
[  876.654321] nvme 0000:01:00.0: failed to reset controller
[  877.000111] kernel: reiserfs: warning: bad block cluster at 0x00f3a2
```
jin: thanks. That `submission timeout` + reset failures lines up with controller-side error recovery loops, not just a single bad sector. Could be thermal/firmware issue aggravated by heavy small writes.
alex: immediate plan I propose: 1) pause cleaner/crons for eu-west2, 2) switch cleaner to low-iops mode (`--rate-limit=5000`) for affected nodes, 3) soft-drain GPUs off hosts and move workloads to warm spare pool, 4) mark devices with >threshold reallocated_count as maintenance, 5) schedule targeted reprovision after sanity checks.
sam: do we need a cross-region emergency capacity bump to absorb batch jobs? I can re-route some burst queues to us-central until stable, but will increase cost.
leah: yes please, reroute opportunistic batch to us-central1 and ap-south as fallback. Set alert to escalate if cross-region usage >15% for >30m.
ops-bot: config-change: scrub cron disabled in eu-west2; gpu-scheduler: avoid allocations to drained nodes; monitoring thresholds lowered for SMART reallocated_count to early warn.
mara: initial impact: IOPS on previously noisy hosts dropped from ~240k -> ~18k within 4m after pausing cleaner. No new reboots in last 12m. We'll hold the drains for one more rotation and run a controlled low-iops scrub later tonight.
jin: action item for follow-up: create ticket in infra/cleanup to add randomized jitter to scrub starts across AZs and cap parallel device scrubs. Also add a soft-rate ramp (10s ramp up) to avoid synchronous microbursts. CC: eng-infra and schedulers.
alex: agreed. Also want a postmortem item: evaluate firmware versions on devices flagged and consider staggered firmware update with canary devices.
sam: cost note for ops: expected extra cross-region egress/compute ~$1.8k for the temporary reroute window if sustained 2h. I'll log to finance and customer-facing CT.
leah: monitoring: setting temporary dashboard tile for eu-west2 nvme reallocated_count and attach-failure-rate + GPU attach latency.
ops-bot: NOTE: scrub disabled, nodes drained, routing rule applied. Monitoring alarms set.
mara: initial green: no new attach errors for 18m, IOPS stable. Will run `nvme smart-log` and `badblocks -n` once we finish verification and post results here.
jin: small improvement proposal: add a pre-scan that checks recent GC write patterns and delays scrub start if a GC burst is detected in the prior 10m window.
alex: good idea. Assigning @mara to coordinate with @jin on the scrub-harness PR. I'll keep the thread updated if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
